Relays remain one of the most vital electrical instruments in modern facilities. These devices are responsible for controlling, isolating, and protecting circuits across a range of critical operations.

Yet, many 
facilities employ relays without adequate consideration
 of the factors that determine long-term performance and reliability. The consequence of overlooking these elements can include equipment failure, operational disruption, and safety hazards.

Importance of Relays in Critical Operations

Relays function as switching devices that connect low-power control systems with high-power circuits. Their role extends beyond basic control, as they incorporate isolation, amplification, and protection within electrical systems.

In environments such as data centers, industrial plants, or healthcare facilities, uninterrupted operation is essential. Any failure in relay performance directly affects sensitive equipment and compromises safety measures. For this reason, specifying relays requires careful evaluation of both technical and operational demands.

Common Oversights during Relay Specification

Despite their importance, engineers often underestimate certain aspects when deploying relays. These oversights can cause premature device wear, inconsistent operation, or even total system breakdown.

Key areas often neglected include:

Contact Ratings and Durability

Facilities sometimes select relays solely based on coil voltage or switching function, ignoring contact ratings. Contact material and endurance under load influence the ability of the relay to handle frequent cycles without deterioration. Inadequate consideration of this factor results in overheating, arcing, or fused contacts that endanger connected devices.

Switching Speed and Response Time

Critical operations rely on precision timing. Relays that lack the required switching speed may cause delays, leading to 
equipment malfunction
 or loss of synchronization. This is especially true in automated systems where millisecond accuracy ensures process safety.

Electrical Isolation and Safety Compliance

Not all relays provide adequate insulation between the control and load circuits. Failure to evaluate insulation strength exposes sensitive instruments to voltage spikes or faults. Overlooking compliance with international safety standards also increases the risk of equipment damage or personnel injury.

Mechanical Wear in Electromechanical Relays

Electromechanical relays
 employ moving parts that wear out over time. Facilities that deploy these devices without assessing operational cycles often face unexpected maintenance needs. Predicting mechanical lifespan is essential for ensuring uninterrupted service.

Temperature and Environmental Conditions

Physical Metal: Full Ownership, Real Costs
ETFs: The Efficient Middle Ground
CFDs: Leverage, Flexibility, and the Cost of Both
Choosing Based on Your Actual Objective
Conclusion

Three people can all say they “invest in gold” and mean completely different things. One holds coins in a home safe. Another owns shares of a fund that tracks the spot price. The third opens leveraged positions on a trading platform and closes them the same day. The return potential, the costs, and the risks of each approach are so different that they barely belong in the same conversation. Choosing between them is not a matter of preference — it is a matter of understanding what you are actually buying and what you are paying for it.

The 
guide to investing in precious metals
 covers the full range of instruments in detail. This article focuses on the three most widely used approaches, what each one actually costs, and where each one fits.

Physical Metal: Full Ownership, Real Costs

Buying physical gold, silver, or platinum means owning the metal outright. No counterparty, no fund manager, no intermediary standing between you and the asset. That is the appeal, and for a specific type of investor with a specific objective — long-term capital preservation with no tolerance for counterparty risk — it is a genuine advantage.

The costs are real and often underestimated. The premium over spot price when buying physical metal ranges from 1-2% for large gold bars to 5-8% for one-ounce coins. Silver coins typically carry premiums of 15-20% over spot because minting and distribution costs are proportionally larger relative to the metal’s value. That premium is an immediate loss the moment you buy. To break even, the spot price has to recover the entire premium before you see any gain.

Storage costs add a recurring drag. A bank safe deposit box runs $50-200 per year depending on size and location. Private vault storage for larger holdings typically costs 0.1-0.15% of value annually. Home storage eliminates fees but introduces security risk and may require additional insurance. Selling physical metal carries another spread: dealers pay below spot when buying back, typically 1-5% below depending on the metal and the form factor.

Physical metal makes most sense for investors who want permanent, unconditional ownership of a real asset and are willing to accept lower liquidity and higher transaction costs as the price of that certainty. It is not an efficient vehicle for trading or for capturing short to medium-term price moves.

Investors often learn from their 
The Gold King
 advisors how holding tangible bullion protects wealth against long-term currency devaluation. Physical precious metals serve as a durable store of value during times of economic turbulence.

ETFs: The Efficient Middle Ground

Precious metal ETFs — exchange-traded funds backed by physical metal held in secure vaults — give investors the economic exposure of physical ownership with the liquidity of a stock. You buy shares through a standard brokerage account, the fund holds the underlying metal on your behalf, and the share price tracks the spot price minus a small annual management fee.

The cost structure is significantly cleaner than physical ownership. The SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD) charges an annual expense ratio of 0.40%. The iShares Gold Trust (IAU) charges 0.25%. Silver equivalents like the iShares Silver Trust (SLV) run at 0.50%. Transaction costs are standard brokerage commissions, typically $0-10 per trade on most platforms. There is no storage cost, no insurance premium, and no buy-sell spread beyond the fund’s expense ratio and the market bid-ask spread, which for major gold ETFs is typically 1-2 cents per share.

The main limitation of ETFs is that they reintroduce a counterparty. The fund custodian holds the physical metal. In a systemic crisis severe enough that people are reaching for physical gold, the reassurance that a fund holds gold in a London vault may feel less certain than a bar you can touch. For most investors in most scenarios, this distinction is theoretical. For the investor specifically trying to hedge against financial system failure, it is not.

ETFs are the right instrument for investors who want genuine precious metal exposure at low cost with full liquidity and no operational complexity. They work for both long-term strategic allocations and medium-term tactical positions.

CFDs: Leverage, Flexibility, and the Cost of Both

A CFD, or contract for difference, is a derivative instrument that lets you speculate on the price movement of a metal without owning it or any fund that holds it. You put up a margin deposit, take a position on whether the price will rise or fall, and settle the difference in cash when you close the trade. LiteFinance offers CFDs on gold, silver, platinum, and palladium, with leverage available that amplifies both gains and losses relative to the margin deployed.

The cost structure of CFDs differs fundamentally from physical metal or ETFs. The upfront cost is the spread — the difference between the buy price and the sell price quoted by the broker. On gold CFDs this is typically 0.3-1.0 points, which sounds small but represents a fixed hurdle the trade has to clear before it becomes profitable. There is no annual expense ratio, but there is an overnight swap rate — a financing charge applied each day a leveraged position is held open. For a long gold position, the daily swap is typically negative, meaning you pay to hold the position overnight. Over weeks and months, swap costs accumulate into a meaningful drag on returns.

CFDs are built for traders, not investors. The leverage that makes them capital-efficient for short-term positions makes them expensive and risky to hold for extended periods. A trader who opens a gold CFD in the morning and closes it the same afternoon pays only the spread. An investor who holds a leveraged CFD position for six months is paying swap costs every night while the position is open. The instrument is not designed for that use case.

Where CFDs genuinely excel is in flexibility. You can take short positions — profiting if metal prices fall — which neither physical metal nor standard ETFs allow. You can use leverage to express a high-conviction short-term view without tying up large amounts of capital. And you can access metals markets with very small account sizes that would not support meaningful physical purchases.

Choosing Based on Your Actual Objective

The right instrument is determined by time horizon and purpose, not by which option sounds most sophisticated.

For long-term capital preservation over five or more years, physical metal or a low-cost ETF is the appropriate instrument. Physical metal if counterparty risk is a genuine concern; ETF if liquidity and cost efficiency matter more. The World Gold Council’s recommendation of 5-15% portfolio allocation to gold applies to both.

For medium-term tactical allocation — a six to eighteen month view on metal prices driven by a macro thesis — ETFs are almost always more efficient than physical metal and more appropriate than CFDs. The holding cost is low, liquidity is high, and there is no overnight financing risk.

For short-term trading, price speculation, or hedging an existing portfolio against a near-term move, CFDs provide leverage and flexibility that the other instruments cannot match. The cost is acceptable for short holding periods and becomes punishing for longer ones.

Conclusion

Physical gold, ETFs, and CFDs all give you exposure to precious metal prices. They do so through completely different mechanisms, at completely different costs, and with completely different risk profiles. Confusing them — buying CFDs when you want long-term capital protection, or buying physical silver when you want to trade momentum — is one of the most common and expensive mistakes new precious metal investors make.

The decision starts with the question of what you are actually trying to achieve. Capital protection over a decade points to physical metal or a low-cost ETF. A tactical allocation over the next year points to an ETF. A short-term trade on a specific price move points to a CFD. Match the instrument to the objective, understand what it costs at each stage, and the choice becomes straightforward.

 and clear trends. Forex pairs like EUR/USD and major stock indices often exhibit predictable patterns, making them suitable for those starting binary trading.

Factors to Consider:

Historical performance

Liquidity and volatility

Timeframes and trading hours

Enhancing Your Skills

Improving as a binary trader involves continuous learning and adapting. Here are some tips to enhance your skills:

Follow Market News
: Stay updated with global economic developments.

Join Trading Communities
: Interact with experienced traders to exchange insights.

Analyze Past Trades
: Review your trading history to identify patterns and areas for improvement.

Binary trading is a journey of constant learning. Dedication to improvement is key to long-term success.

Understanding Expiry Times in Binary Trading

Of all the elements that shape binary trading, the most fundamental is probably expiry times. The expiry time is already specified while your trade is active up to the time it is going to close. After this, the fate of the trade will be determined: will it end up in profit or loss? This is precisely why expiry times act as the most important element in determining a strategy that will be used by most traders, particularly beginners who have not yet learned the trading rules of the stock market.

There is really no overstating the necessity of the proper selection of an expiry time. For example, short-term expiry, say 
between 60 seconds and 5 minutes
, is very interesting to those who want quick results and a fast pace in trading.

These short-term durations force you to have knee-jerk reactions to rapid market movements and thus would be more applicable to persons who can best handle these different levels of risk and stress. Such types of trades can be great, indeed, regarded as very erratic and very closely planned, to the point that almost no error margin exists since most decisions need to be made in seconds.

In contrast, for a person with a long expiry time of hours to days or even longer, the trading would be quite relaxed. It allows all rounds of market analysis, be it technical analysis or general market trends.

The Role of Emotions in Binary Trading

There isn’t much to say about the effects that emotions have had on binary trading. All of them divert decision-making from logical reasoning and well-defined frameworks. Trading is not only the test of financial knowledge but also that of emotional endurance. The most common emotional traps that wreck even the most well-prepared plans are those of fear and greed.

Fear causes traders to doubt their decisions and leads them to an early exit from trades and even sometimes deny themselves lucrative opportunities. Instead, greed leads to overtrading without pronounced factors that compel action, so risks are taken on with little thought and stakes raised irrationally, all for the pursuit of easy profits.

These emotions are naturally normal, especially for a fresh trader who may be facing uncertainties or volatility in the market. These unreasonable emotions create impulsive decisions, while the end is to achieve growing losses and frustrations associated with them. An example is when fear develops from previous losses or the inability to tell the market where it is likely headed, while greed usually originates from excitement from recent winners or unrealistic expectations for gains.

The Importance of Tracking and Analyzing Trades

Keeping a detailed record of your trades is a fundamental practice for achieving long-term success in binary trading. Each trade you execute carries valuable information about your decision-making process, market conditions, and the effectiveness of your strategies.

By tracking each trade, you gain a clearer understanding of what works and what doesn’t, enabling you to identify patterns that lead to profits or losses. This habit is especially critical for beginners, as they are still in the early stages of developing their trading skills and learning how to navigate the complexities of the market.

Analyzing past trades goes beyond simply reviewing results. It helps traders recognize consistent strengths and weaknesses, offering insights into the strategies and market conditions that align best with their approach.

Final Thoughts

Starting binary trading can be a rewarding venture if approached with the right mindset and preparation. For beginners, understanding market dynamics, choosing a reliable broker, and practicing on demo accounts are essential first steps. With a disciplined strategy and effective risk management, you can navigate the market confidently.

Whether you’re exploring binary options for beginners or seeking advanced strategies, remember that patience and continuous learning are your greatest assets. By taking a structured approach and staying committed to improvement, you can unlock the potential of this exciting trading method.

Saudi Capital Market Authority (CMA) has proposed allowing foreign nationals from GCC countries or those previously residing in Saudi Arabia or GCC countries to invest in the Saudi stock market. 

This would also enable
 individuals who previously lived in Saudi Arabia or the GCC to continue operating their investment accounts after returning home, provided they opened an account in Saudi Arabia.

Yellow and Black Markings
White and Black Markings
Blue and Black Markings

In Saudi Arabia, the colors of footpath markings indicate where drivers can and cannot park. Understanding these colors can help you avoid traffic violations and fines. Here’s a quick guide to what each color means:

Yellow and Black Markings

No Parking⛔:
 The yellow and black markings on the footpath in Saudi Arabia indicate areas where parking is strictly prohibited. Drivers should avoid stopping or parking their vehicles in these zones to prevent traffic obstructions and potential penalties.

White and Black Markings

Parking Allowed 🅿️:
 The white and black markings on the footpath in Saudi Arabia indicate areas where you can park your car. They are designated for general parking, providing a safe vehicle space without disrupting traffic flow.

Red Markings

Emergency Vehicles 🚑:
 Red markings on the footpath in Saudi Arabia means that the place is reserved exclusively for emergency vehicles, such as ambulances, fire trucks, and police cars. 

Private vehicles cannot park in these zones to ensure emergency responders have clear access when needed.

Blue and Black Markings

Paid Parking 🅿:
 Blue and Black markings on the footpath in Saudi Arabia show that these areas are designated for paid parking. Drivers must adhere to local payment regulations to secure a spot in these zones, including using parking meters, mobile apps, or pre-paid parking cards.

Understanding the meanings of footpath colors makes parking in Saudi Arabia easier and safer. Always check the footpath color before parking to ensure you’re in the correct area and avoid fines.

The Saudi government amended 47 articles of Saudi Labor Law in August 2024, which will become effective in February 2025. We have explained the significant amendments below;

Death Leave

In case of the death of a sibling (brother or sister), the worker is entitled to a leave of 3 fully paid working days as per Article 113 of Saudi Labor Law. 

Old: 1 fully paid working day. 

10 types of leaves in Saudi Labor Law
.

Maternity Leave

Every Saudi and expat working woman in Saudi Arabia is entitled to 12 weeks of fully paid maternity leave as per Article 151 of Saudi Labor Law. 

Old: 10 weeks of maternity leave.

Rules for Maternity Leave in Saudi Arabia
.

Renewal of a Fixed-Term Contract

The employment contract with a non-Saudi will always be 
fixed-term
 as per Article 37 of Saudi Labor Law.

If the employment contract does not mention a period, it is valid for one year from the date of joining. 

If the fixed-term employment contract has no renewal clause, it will be extended for one year.

Old: It will be extended until the Iqama expiry date.

Notice period in a fixed-term contract

To resign or terminate a 
fixed-term contract
, the employee or employer must issue a notice period as mentioned
. If the notice period is not written in the contract, 

The employee must give a 30-day prior notice.

The employer must give a 60-day prior notice.

Notice Period under Saudi Labor Law
.

Probation Period

The 
probation period in Saudi Arabia
 cannot exceed 180 days in any circumstances.

Overtime

The employee can take an 
overtime allowance
 or paid leave for the extra hours worked. 

Source: 
HRSD Ministry
.

Saudi Arabia has raised the retirement age to 65 for both public and private sector workers, up from 60, as part of its Vision 2030 reform plans. 

The decision, approved by the Saudi Cabinet in the latest meeting chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, aims to ensure a sustainable lifestyle for citizens after retirement and improve the conditions of retirees.

Gradual Implementation

The new retirement age will be implemented gradually, with a four-month increase in retirement age for each month until the new age limit is reached. 

This policy will apply to workers under 48 years and 6 months old when the decision is issued. 

The retirement age of those individuals who are already 58 years and 4 months old at the time of this decision will not change.

Meanwhile, younger workers, specifically those under 29 years of age at the time of the policy implementation, will see their retirement age set at 65 years.

Termination/Resignation at Retirement Age

As a result, the employer cannot terminate an employee at 60 under Article 74 (4) of Saudi Labor Law. The employer will have to wait five more years now, as the retirement age has increased to 65.

As per 
Article 74 of Saudi Labor Law
, an employee can resign, and the employer can terminate the contract at retirement age without 
any penalty
. It means that;

The employee will receive the full 
End of Service Benefits
 if he resigns at the retirement age in KSA.

Similarly, the employer will not have to pay any additional benefit to the employee for termination at the retirement age.

If the employment contract goes beyond the retirement age, it can be terminated at the 
contract completion date.

Saudi environmental authorities have warned sternly against cultivating “invasive” plants due to their damaging impact on the delicate ecosystem. 

The Saudi government has announced that if someone is found growing invasive plants at their home, farm, or any other place, he will be fined SR 10,000/plant.

Why are they banned?

These invasive species are known for their rapid growth and abundant seed production, which allows them to spread through the assistance of birds, animals, and wind. They pose a significant threat to the native vegetation. 

Many people do not know that even an aloe vera plant is an invasive plant.

Famous Invasive Plants

Fifty-two exotic species have been documented in Saudi Arabia, with some having entered and become naturalized in the Kingdom several decades ago. Among these, 44 are from the American continents, four are from tropical countries, two are from Australia, and one is from East Asia, South Asia, and Iran.

All major invasive species in Saudi Arabia are native to the American continent. The following species potentially damage biodiversity or alter ecosystems in general.

 Aloe vera.

Argemone ochrolecuca.

Nicotiana glauca.

Opuntia dellenii.

O. ficus-indica.

Prosopis juliflora.

Trianthema portulacastrum. 

Source:

A viral social media video has yet allowed for another arrest. In the video, a man is seen feeding an SR 500 note to a camel. The currency note was real and was deliberately given to the camel.

Types of Contract
Resignation – Fixed Term Contract
At the end of the contract
During the contract period
Resignation – Indefinite Contract

If you resign from your job during contract period in Saudi Arabia, follow this to avoid the rejection of your resignation by the employer. We have explained the resignation rules as per Saudi Labor Law below. 

How to resign in Qiwa?

Types of Contract

There are two kinds of contracts as per Saudi Labor Law and the resignation rules largely differ depending upon the type of the contract. 

Fixed-Term Contract.

Indefinite Contract.

Every employee be it it a Saudi or an expat signs a fixed-term contract in the beginning with his employer in Saudi Arabia. 

A contract with a Saudi employee becomes an indefinite contract after some time period. 

However, a contract with a Non-Saudi employee will always remain a fixed-term contract as per Article 37 of Saudi Labor Law.

 Expatriate Employees = Fixed Term Contract.

Saudi Employees = Fixed-term or indefinite contract.

Resignation – Fixed Term Contract

At the end of the contract

An employee can resign 
at the end of a fixed-term contract
 
as specified under 
Article 74 of Saudi Labor Law
 by giving a sufficient 
notice period.

But 
what is the expiry of your contract
? Normally, the expiry date is written explicitly in the contract but upon renewal, people get confused which date to consider as the completion date.

If there is a
 renewal clause with a specified period
 in the fixed-term contract, the contract will be renewed for the time period mentioned in the contract as per Article 55 (2) of Saudi Labor Law.

If there is 
no renewal clause
 in the fixed-term contract or the time period is not specified,

Non-Saudis:
 The contract will be renewed to the 
date of the Iqama expiry
 for an expat employee as per Article 37 of Saudi Labor Law.

Saudis: 
If the employer does not terminate a Saudi employee, the contract will be renewed and become an indefinite contract.

During the contract period

If you want to 
resign during a fixed-term contract period
 before its completion in Saudi Arabia, make sure that your employer fully agrees to that. The employer has the right to reject your resignation in Saudi Arabia or 
ask for compensation 
under 
Article 77 of Saudi Labor Law
.

Therefore, if your employer rejects your resignation in Saudi Arabia, it is better to weigh the compensation you might have to pay with the salary increment you are getting by changing the job. 

Resignation – Indefinite Contract

An employee can resign from job with an indefinite contract with a 60-day 
notice period
 under Article 75 of Saudi Labor Law.

If an employee resigns under an indefinite contract, the employer has the right to ask for penalty compensation under 
Article 77 of Saudi Labor Law
.

It is important to reiterate that Non-Saudi employees cannot have an indefinite contract as per Article 37 of Saudi Labor Law.

Definition of Indefinite Contract

For Saudi employees, a fixed-term contract becomes an indefinite contract under the following 2 conditions;

If there is no renewal clause in the fixed-term contract and the employer does not terminate the employee at the contract completion, it will become an indefinite contract in Saudi Arabia.

A fixed-term contract becomes an indefinite contract after 3 consecutive renewals, or after 4 years of service as per article 55 (2) of Saudi Labor Law.

Source: 
Saudi Labor Law

Ayat Kareema was the dua of

Benefits of Ayat Kareema

Ayat Kareema is such a powerful dua that Allah made it a part of the Holy Quran. Here are some of its benefits;

Problem Solver

The most significant benefit of repeating Ayat Kareema is that for whatever reason a Muslim recites it, Allah listens to him and resolves his problems. It is also evident in a Hadith.

As-Saffat 37:144

Financial Issues

Are you struggling with financial issues due to unexpected job loss, business failure, or loss of money? If so, you may find solace in reciting Ayat Kareema. 

This powerful prayer, when recited in a prescribed manner, is believed to help overcome financial difficulties and provide relief during trying times. Give it a try and see if it can help alleviate your financial stress.

Forgives for Sins

The story of Prophet Yunus عليه السلام also gave us a lesson that one of the best ways to ask for forgiveness for your sins from Allah is by reciting Ayat Kareema. 

Curing life-threatening disease

Ayat e Karima is a powerful Islamic prayer that, when recited with unwavering faith, can bring about miraculous healing.  Al-Hill,

.

Someone coming to Jeddah with the intention to stay in the city for

 would be considered a Muqeem of Jeddah from the very first day, and therefore, he will not be praying for

Ayat-ul-Kursi – Arabic Text

اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَّهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ

Ayat-ul-Kursi – English translation

Allah – there is no God except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. 

Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep.

To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.

Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?

He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills.

An expat filed a case against a company for setting Huroob against him without any valid reason just to avoid payment of dues. He finally won the case, along with SR 1.75 million dues + lawyers’ fee.

5 new rules to remove Huroob

Performing Tawaf is one of the fard acts of Hajj and Umrah. In Tawaf, Muslims walk around the Holy Kaaba for 7 times in a particular way. Although it is not a Sunnah, but the following 7 Duas are recommended for the 7 rounds of Tawaf for Muslims.

.

It is better to make your own supplications while performing Tawaf as it is one of those 
places in Masjid al-Haram where all duas are accepted

Dua – 1st round of Tawaf

اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْتَلْكَ بِاسْمِكَ الَّذِي يُمُشَى بِهِ عَلَى طَلَلِ الْمَاءِ كَمَا يُمُشی بِهِ عَلى جُدَدِ الْأَرْضِ وَ اَسْئَلُكَ بِاسْمِكَ الَّذِي يَهْتَزُّ لَهُ عَرْشُكَ وَ اَسْتَلْكَ الَّذِي تَهْتَزُّ لَهُ أَقْدَامُ مَلَائِكَتِكَ وَ أَسْمُلَكَ بِاسْمِكَ الَّذِي دَعَاكَ بِهِ مُوسَى مِنْ جَانِبِ الطُّورِ فَاسْتَجَبْتَ لَهُ وَ الْقَيْتَ عَلَيْهِ مَحَبَّةٌ مِنْكَ وَ اسْتَلْكَ بِاسْمِكَ الَّذِي غَفَرْتَ بِهِ لِمُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ آلِهِ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ وَ مَا تَاَخَرَ وَ أَتْمَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ نِعْمَتَكَ أن تَرزُقَنِي خَيْرُ الدُّنْيَا وَالآخِرة.

O Allah! I call on you by your name, by which it is walked on the waves of the seas as it is walked on the roads of the land, 
And I call on you by your name, for which your throne shakes, 
And I call on you by your name, for which the feet of your angels tremble, 
And I call on you by your name by which 
Prophet Musa
 عليه السلام prayed to you from the side of the Mountain Toor and you accepted his prayer and conferred your love on him, 
And I call on you by your name by which you pardoned Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his household, all his previous and future sins, and completed all thine blessings for him 
to provide me with the best of this world and the hereafter.

Dua – 2nd round of Tawaf

للّهُمَّ إِنِّى إِلَيْكَ فَقِيرٌ وَإِنِّى خَائِفٌ مُسْتَجِيم تغَيِّرُ جِسْمِي وَلَا تُبَدِّلُ إِسْمِي فلا سَائِلُكَ فَقِيرُكَ مِسْكِيْنُكَ بِبَابِكَ فَتَصَدَّقُ عَلَيْهِ بِالْجَنَّةِ اللَّهُمَّ الْبَيْتُ بَيْتُكَ وَ الْحَرَمُ حَرَمُكَ وَ الْعَبْدُ عَبْدُكَ وَ هَذَا مَقَامُ الْعَائِدِ الْمُسْتَجِيرِ بِكَ مِنَ وَهَذَا النَّارِ فَاعْتِقْنِي وَ وَالِدَيَّ وَأَهْلِي وَ وُلدِي وَ اِخْوَانِيَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنَ النَّارِ يَا جَوَادُ يَا كَرِيم

O Allah! I am your dependent servant, and I am fearful and take refuge in you; so do not alter my body nor change my name. I am your beggar, your poor destitute servant at your gate; so grant me mercifully your paradise.

O Allah! The House is your House, and the sanctuary is your sanctuary, and the servant is your servant, and this is the station of him who turns to you and takes refuge with you from Fire; 
so save me and my parents, my children and my faithful brethren from Fire, for your art the Generous, the Gracious.

Dua – 3rd round of Tawaf

اللَّهُمَّ ادْخِلْنِي الجَنَّةَ وأجرى مِنَ النَّارِ برحمتك أَجِرْنِي بِرَحْمَتِكَ وَعَافِنِي مِنَ السُّقْمِ وَ أَوْسِعُ عَلَيَّ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ الْحَلَالِ وَادْرَهُ عَنِّى شَرَّ فَسَقَةِ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ وَ شَرَّ فَسَقَةِ الْعَرَبِ وَ الْعَجَمِ يَا ذَا الْمَنِّ وَالطَّولِ يَا ذَا الْجُودِ وَ الْكَرَمِ إِنَّ عَمَلِى ضَعِيفٌ فَضَاعِفُهُ لِى تَقَبَّلُهُ مِنِّي إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيم

O Allah! 
Grant me the Jannah by your mercy, and give me refuge from Fire by your mercy, and heal me from disease, 
and enlarge your lawful bounty for me, and keep me safe from the evil of the dissolute among the genies and men and the evil of the Arabs and non-Arabs.

O you bountiful, mighty and munificent! 
My deed is little, so multiply it, and accept it from me; verily you are the All-hearing, the All-knowing.

Dua – 4th round of Tawaf

يَا اللَّهُ يَا وَلِيَّ الْعَافِيَةِ وَ خَالِقَ الْعَافِيَةِ وَ رَازِقَ الْعَافِيَةِ وَالْمُنْعِمُ بِالْعَافِيَةِ وَالْمُتَفَضِّلُ بِالْعَافِيَةِ م عَلَيَّ وَعَلَى جَمِيعَ خَلْقِكَ يَا رَحُمْنَ الدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ وَ رَحِيْمَهُمَا صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَارْزُقْنَا الْعَافِيَةَ وَ تَمَامَ الْعَافِيَةِ وَ شُكْرَ الْعَافِيَةِ فِي الدُّنيا وَ الْآخِرَةِ يَا أَرْحَمَ الرَّاحِمِينَ

O Allah! The owner of well-being, the creator of well-being, the bestower of well-being, the granter of well-being, and the conferrer of well-being on me and on all your creatures, 
O, you the merciful of this world and the hereafter and their compassionate God, b
less Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his household, and bestow on us well-being, full well-being, and thanks giving on well-being in this world and the hereafter, by your mercy, O you most merciful.

Dua – 5th round of Tawaf

الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي شَرَّفَكِ وَعَظَمَكِ وَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي بَعَثَ مُحَمَّدًا نَبِيًّا وَجَعَلَ عَلِيًّا إِمَامًا اَللهُمَّ اهْدِ لَهُ خِيَارَ خَلْقِكَ وَ جَيْبُهُ شِرَارَ خَلْقِكَ رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَّ فِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَّ قِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ –

Praise to Allah Who has honored us and exalted us, Praise to Allah Who sent Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as a prophet and designated Ali as Imam and the leader. O, Allah, Guide the best of your people to him, and keep the evil of your creatures away from him.

O our Lord, Grant us your blessing in this world and your blessing in the other world, and save us from the pain of Fire.

Dua – 6th round of Tawaf

اللَّهُمَّ الْبَيْتُ بَيْتُكَ وَالْعَبْدُ عَبْدُكَ وَهَذَا مَقَامُ الْعَالِدِيكَ مِنَ النار اللهم من قبلك الروح و الْفَرْجُ وَ الْعَافِيَةُ اَللّهُمَّ إِنَّ عَمَلِى ضَعِيفٌ فَضَاعِفُهُ لِى وَ اغْفِرُ لِى مَا اطَّلَعْتَ عَلَيْهِ مِنِّي وَ خَفِيَ عَلَى خَلْقِكَ أَسْتَجِيرُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ النَّارِ –

O Allah! The House is your House, and this is the station of him who takes refuge with you from Fire. O Allah! All blessing, relief and well-being come from you.

O Allah! My deed is little, so multiply it for me, and forgive all that you know of me but has been hidden from your creatures. I take refuge with Allah from Fire.

Dua – 7th round of Tawaf

اللهم إن عِندِى أَفْوَاجًا مِن ذُنُوبِ وَأَفْوَاجًا من خَطَايَا وَعِندَكَ افواج مِنْ رَحْمَةٍ و أفواج من مِنْ مَغْفِرَةٍ يَا مَنِ اسْتَجَابَ لِاَبْغَضِ خَلْقِهِ إِذْ قَالَ انْظِرْنِي إِلَى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ اسْتَجِبْ لِي – ـعُنِى بِمَا رَزَقْتَنِى وَبَارِكْ لِى فِيْمَا آتَيْتَنِى.

O Allah! I bear crowds of sins and crowds of faults, and with you are crowds of blessing and crowds of forgiveness. O you Who granted the request of your most hated creatures when he said “give me respite until the day they are resurrected,” grant me my request. When he said,” Give me time to the day of resurrection, accept from me. O Allah! Make me content with what you have provided me with, and bless me with what you have given me.

Ever wondered why WhatsApp audio and video calling is banned in Saudi Arabia? We have covered the basic reasons here.

 Caller’s Identity

According to Samir Al-Junaid, a Saudi technology expert, WhatsApp video and audio calls are banned in Saudi Arabia due to the reason that the caller identification can be faked. The only condition to open these calls is to assure that the caller is not fake.

The only condition that the Saudi Communications Authority has imposed on the calls-over-the-internet is they shall ensure real and identifiable identity of the caller.

In the wake of hygiene, Saudi Arabia has put forward a new list of municipal fines that shall be imposed on restaurants, shops, contractors, workers, and individuals. We have explained the new penalties imposed below.

Fines on restaurants and cafes

Staff caught picking their nose, spitting, touching their mouth, or exhibiting poor personal hygiene will be fined SR 400 to SR 2,000.

Fines range from SR 400 to SR 2,000 on workers displaying symptoms of illness, wounds, or blisters.

Employers who hire workers without a valid health certificate or with an expired/incorrect one will be subject to fines ranging from SR 400 to SR 2,000.

Fines for low hygiene standards in toilets, presence of pests, unclean appliances, and unsterilized equipment can result in penalties ranging from SR 400 to SR 2,000.

Tobacco sales violations

It is prohibited by law to sell tobacco products to people under 18. Moreover, it is essential to be equipped with a license to get involved in tobacco sales. 

Those not equipped with necessary licenses or found guilty of selling to people under 18 years of age shall be fined in the range from SR 1,000 to SR 5,000.

Gas stations and petroleum violations

The gas station needs to sell appropriate fuels. Selling non-compliant or mixed fuels would result in fines ranging from 1,000 to 10,000 riyals.

Licensing and business regulations

If any 
business
 is operational yet does not possess a municipal license, it shall receive a fine ranging from SR 10,000 to SR 50,000. 

If a business has a license yet is practicing what is not within the permissible range of the license, then the fine would be from 400 to SR 5,000.

Road and public space violations

Those contractors who do not comply with the regulations related to drilling, waste disposal, and public property shall also face heavy fines ranging from SR 200 to 50,000.

Building and construction violations

Any building that is under construction or is being demolished without a license shall also be subjected to a fine. Also, any construction activity beyond the building permit limits shall face fines. These are hefty fines, such as SR 50,000.

Medical facilities and health practitioners

Several fines have been imposed on medical facilities. Thus, those medical facilities or practitioners who do not comply with health requirements, dispose of the medical waste properly, or misuse the medical devices can face fines ranging from SR 2,000 to SR 50,000.

Source: 
Gulf News

Saudi Citizens and Iqama holders can go to Jail if their child stays absent from school for 20 days without a valid reason. 

Why such a rule?

This law ensures that all children living in Saudi Arabia have the fundamental right to education. It also means that parents must send their children to school. They cannot keep them away from the school by their choice.

What is the process? 

Saudi child protection law states that the guardians shall be inquired if they cannot send their child to school for 20 days or more. 

The school principal must report the absentee cases to the education department so that the inquiry against the parents/guardians can occur.

The criminal investigation arrested an expat for possessing unregistered veterinarian medicines in Dammam.

What was his crime?

According to the criminal investigation officers, the culprit was transporting veterinary preparations in a vehicle without refrigerators, heat maps, and temperature gauges, even though the country was observing high temperatures.

The sources confirm that the Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) has referred the worker to Public Prosecution. The Saudi press agency reported that the worker was arrested during the inspection tour of the officials in the city of Dammam.

Unregistered medicine

The authority also claimed that the worker was equipped with unregistered veterinary medicinal preparations. He used raw materials to process veterinary medicines such as sprays. 

It is indicated that he was manufacturing sprays used to treat parasites and animals’ eye diseases.

The investigation team analysis showed that the technical regulations for manufacturing veterinarian medicines were not complied with.

The worker also had in possession empty containers for the purpose of filling these preparations without obtaining regular licenses.

Article 27 Veterinary Products Law

The SFDA stipulates that the veterinary preparation’s possession, manufacture, composition, and marketing should be done only after attaining necessary statutory licenses by the Veterinary Products Law in the Gulf Cooperation Council states and executed according to Article 27 of the law.

Expected Punishment

This article states that for anyone who violates the preparation, sales, and manufacturing rules, SFDA has the right to refer them to the Public Prosecution. 

The law also states that the penalty for violation is imprisonment for five years and a fine not exceeding SR 5 million or both.

What is the Day of Khullaif?
Cleaning Masjid al-Haram
Providing Food
Guarding the Houses

This beautiful annual custom of the people of Makkah 🕋 on the day of Arafah is called the “
day of the Khullaif
,” 
يوم الخُلّيف
 and it has been practiced for many years.

Khullaif is an Arabic word from “Takhallaf,” which means someone who missed out or failed to do something.

What is the Day of Khullaif?

When the men of Makkah are performing Hajj and go out with the pilgrims to Arafat to help, the women of Makkah, the boys, and the elderly go out to Masjid Al Haram to perform Tawaf around the Kaaba so that the Haram does not remain deserted.

The visitors on the day of Hajj at the Grand mosque are those who do not perform Hajj and thus are usually women, kids, and the elderly. These visitors thus stay in the mosque from Fajr to Isha prayers.

The day of Khulliaf marks availing of the opportunity by the women of Makkah to perform Umrah and take care of Masjid al-Haram.

Cleaning Masjid al-Haram

On the day of Khullaif, women even clean the Grand Mosque, as they know that the Hajj pilgrims will return for Tawaf on the third day.

Providing Food

Moreover, the people who do not perform Hajj follow the sunnah of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ of keeping fast on the day of Arafah. Thus, these women bring food for those who observe the fast to accompany them when they break their fast.

Guarding the Houses

In the past, on the day of Khullaif, women would help the elderly. They would provide them with food, water, and assistance. They would also guard the houses of those who have left for Hajj.

Source: 
Saudi Gazette

To authorize someone to sell your property in Pakistan, you must give a power of attorney (PoA) duly attested by the embassy or consulate. 

Executant: The person who is giving the PoA.

Attorney: The person who is authorized to sell your property.

Writing the Power of Attorney

First of all, contact a lawyer back in Pakistan to draft a power of attorney for you with a specific purpose, such as selling a particular property. 

Although you can get help from petition writers sitting in front of the Pakistan Embassy or Consulate, hiring a professional lawyer is better. 

Witness Signatures

The lawyer will email you the draft power of attorney which you need to print for attestation from the Pakistan Embassy or consulate. 

Write the names and the CNIC numbers of two witnesses who know you personally and get the document signed by them. 

Required Documents

You need to bring 
two sets
 of the following documents with you to the Pakistan Embassy or Consulate to attest a power of attorney;

Proof of Ownership of the property (Fard, Registration deed, inheritance certificate).

Original CNIC + copy of the executant.

Copy of Saudi Iqama of the executant.

Saudi mobile number of the executant.

Two passport-sized photographs of the executant.

CNIC copy of the Attorney.

Pakistani mobile number of the attorney. 

CNIC copies of two witnesses.

Visit Pakistan Embassy

After arranging the above-mentioned required documents, visit the petition writers sitting in front of the Pakistan Embassy or consulate at around 10 am.

They will help you fill out other forms, impose a red stamp on your documents and arrange for them to be presented to the embassy against the 
SR 15 fee
. 

 Visit the attestation office in the embassy or consulate and present the power of attorney and the related documents on the counter. 

Present original CNIC or passport for identity verification. 

Sign a power of attorney in front of the consular officer. 

Impose the thumb impressions in front of the consular officer.

Pay the attestation fee of 
SR 18
.

Collecting the documents

The consular officer will ask you to wait around 
1 hour
 to complete the attestation. Once your document is ready, he will call your name to get the documents. 

You will find an electronic power of attorney printed by the consular officer along with an attested set of documents. 

Make sure to 
check
 the following details in the electronic power of attorney before you leave the embassy or consulate;

Name and Father Name of the Executant. 

CNIC Number of the Executant. 

Name and Father Name of the Attorney.

CNIC Number of the Attorney.

Sending documents to Pakistan

My lawyer advised me to send the attested power of attorney to Pakistan and the property’s registration documents only through the 
courier service
. 

The attorney will have to visit Pakistan Foreign Office to ratify the document. The foreign office does not ratify any document without proof that the document has been dispatched through the courier service.

The validity of the Power of Attorney is 
120 days
.

Canceling the power of attorney

If you want to cancel the power of attorney after it is attested, you need to bring all the above-mentioned documents to the Pakistan Embassy or Consulate and follow a similar process for cancellation.

There are 2 Surahs in the Holy Quran that different Sheikhs recommend reciting for rizq, wealth, success, and to avoid money problems.

13 ways to increase your Rizq in Islam

Surah Fajr

Reciting Surah Fajr is recommended by spiritual healers to avoid problems related to the scarcity of Rizq, wealth, success, and money. If you read its meaning, it is a perfect recipe to escape financial trouble.

How to Recite? 

It should be recited after the Fajr Prayer to seek benefit from Allah.

The reader should focus on its meaning to understand what Allah is trying to say in this chapter.

Say dua asking for Allah’ Rehma because Allah accepts the dua after every good deed and Qur’an recitation.

Why Surah Fajr?

Surah Fajr is highly effective for wealth and provisions rizq due to its focus on critical issues that often hinder individuals from enjoying the blessings of abundance. Allah addresses these issues in the Surah;

Ingratitude

And as for man, when his Lord tries him and [thus] is generous to him and favors him, he says, “My Lord has honored me.” – 
Fajr 89:15

Gratitude increases blessings, while neglecting to thank Allah can lead to their decrease.

Entitled Attitude

But when He tests them by limiting their provision, they protest, “My Lord has ˹undeservedly˺ humiliated me!” – 
Fajr 89:16

Verse 16 exposes the flawed mindset of feeling entitled to blessings. When individuals experience a decrease in wealth due to their ingratitude and mistakes, they complain instead of gracefully accepting their situation. Recognizing that everything is a gift from Allah is crucial.

Neglecting the Orphan

Absolutely not! In fact, you are not ˹even˺ gracious to the orphan.
 – 
Fajr 89:17

Verse 17 emphasizes the importance of honoring and supporting orphans. This includes providing moral, emotional, and financial assistance.

Neglecting the Poor

nor do you urge one another to feed the poor. – 
Fajr 89:18

Verse 18 emphasizes the significance of feeding and supporting the needy. Initiating a charity campaign and seeking Allah’s help in this endeavor is vital.

Money as a Deity

Verse 20 warns against making money the center of one’s life. Treating wealth as a deity leads to its control over individuals. Instead, one should appreciate Allah’s blessings and avoid prioritizing wealth over spiritual values.

By addressing these issues and implementing the teachings of Surah Fajr, individuals can cultivate gratitude, support the needy, and avoid the pitfalls that hinder the blessings of wealth and rizq in their lives.

Surah Waqiah 

Many Islamic scholars recommend those who want to increase rizq wealth, success and reduce money problems, and protect against poverty and debt recite Surah Waqia.

How to Recite?

Muslims believe reciting surah Waqiah after the Maghrib prayer can benefit them financially.
 This is why this surah is recited as a supplication to increase wealth. 

Focusing on its meaning and understanding its translation is beneficial when reciting Surah Waqiah as part of our daily recitation.

Why Surah Waqia?

Surah Waqiah emphasizes the importance of gratitude in several of its verses, aligning with Allah’s promise in Surah Ibrahim (Verse 7) that appreciation leads to an increase. 

If you are grateful, I will certainly give you more. – 
Ibrahim 14:7

Gratitude acts as a magnet for blessings, as it is part of Allah’s divine law that when we appreciate Him for what we have, He multiplies those blessings in our lives.

By deeply internalizing the verses in our own language through regular recitation, we begin to cultivate a mindset that attracts financial abundance and shields us from various economic challenges such as poverty, unemployment, debt, and scarcity of resources.

Conclusion

To conclude, the two surahs emphasize the importance of gratitude in most of their verses. Hence by immersing ourselves in the teachings of these two surahs and actively practicing gratitude for our existing financial resources, regardless of their magnitude, we can witness firsthand the increase and blessings bestowed upon them.

Stage One: Autolysis
Stage Two: Bloat
Stage Three: active decay
Stage Four: Skeletonization Decay

As soon as the person dies, the human body starts to decay. This decomposition starts within 5 minutes of the death of the person. Slowly and gradually the human body turns into a skeleton and then into nothing. 

Some bodies tend to decay faster than others: the reason being the varying factors such as the weather, temperature, moisture, pH, and oxygen levels, cause of death, and body position.

Stage One: Autolysis

This is the first step of decomposition where the self-digestion of the human body begins. As soon as the heart stops working and the blood circulation is halted, the oxygen supply to the body ends. This causes the excess carbon dioxide to acidify the body. The toxic environment of the body causes the membranes to release their enzymes and muscle to get stiff.

This causes the skin to get loose and small blisters to start to appear either on both internal or external organs.

Stage Two: Bloat

As the membranes start to release the enzymes, gases are produced inside the body. The production of sulfur and sulfur-containing enzymes causes the skin to change its color. The gas production can cause the size of the body to enhance. The insects can also become active in the body.

The bacterial activity would cause the body to give out an unpleasant smell which is known as putrefaction. The reason why the places such as crime scenes where the murder took place smell so bad is bacterial activity on the body. The place where the murder has taken place and the body remained there for days tends to give a smell even after washing it properly.

Stage Three: active decay

The active fluids of the body start to release in the third stage of decomposition. This stage tends to turn the body into a liquid: the muscles, organs, and skin start to change their state and turn into liquid. What is left after this stage is only hair, cartilage, bones, and the byproducts of decomposition.

Stage Four: Skeletonization Decay

A body can reach this stage either within three weeks or after years. This depends upon the conditions where the body is kept or buried. By the end of the fourth stage, what is left of the human body is disarticulated bones.

Shaddad bin Aad was the king of the lost Arabian city named the Iram of the pillars. Shaddad

When ‘Aad’ died, he left behind two sons Shaddad and Shadeed. After some time Shadeed also died and Shaddad became the ruler of his kingdom. It is said that he was said to have ruled 1,000 Adite tribes. Iram of pillars is known as the city of idols.

 عليه السلام delivered Allah’s message to Shaddad, he asked what would he get in return if he embraces Islam. Prophet Hud عليه السلام explained to him that he would get paradise.

Opening ceremony of the paradise

It took Shaddad 300 years to complete the paradise. Finally, when it was completed, he gave orders to all people to proceed to the walls of the dazzling city of high and magnificent pillars referred to in the Holy Quran as well.

Did you not see how your Lord dealt with Aad, the people of Iram—with ˹their˺ great stature? –

When Shaddad was going to his paradise for the first time, he saw a deer with a trunk and legs of gold and silver. He decided to chase it on his horse and got separated from his army.

Olives and olive oil are widely consumed in Saudi Arabia but not many know that there are several types of olives. Here are some of the best types of olives available in the market. 

6 fruits mentioned in Quran
.

Kalamata

The deep purple and shiny Olives from Greece popularly known as the Kalamata are the most famous type of olives. This Olive is rich in taste which is smoky and fruity. Most people like it raw as a seasoning on salads, some prefer baking or roasting them with meat and veggies.

Castelvetrano

The most famous olives in Italy are the Casteletranos. These are bright green and are widely used as a snack. They are known to have a sweet taste and a unique buttery texture. They belong to the variety of nocerella del belice. They have a mild taste and make a great snack.

Cerignola

These olives drive their name from the place they are harvested. Cerignola is a place in the Puglia region of Italy. Cerignola olives are big in size and have a green color. They have a crisp and buttery taste. Due to their big size, they are usually stuffed with cheese, capers, and garlic!

Nyon

Hailing from France, Nyon has a deep black and subtle bitterness. They are first dried and then aged in brine. They are packed with rosemary and thyme to enrich with aromatic flavors. To enhance their taste, use them with Provençal olive oil.

Niçoise

These black-colored olives hail from France and have an assertive taste. They are used famously in the salade Niçoise and tapenade. However, they are good on their own as well as their taste is not overpowering.

Liguria

They have a great appealing color which is green and black. Grown in Italy, they have a rich taste. They are harvested in northwest Italy in a region called Liguria. Bay leaves, rosemary, and thymes are used to improve the flavor of these small-sized olives.

Gaeta

Another beauty of Italy is Gaeta. It has a purplish-brown color and is soft, moist, and tender from the inside. They are usually dried-cured, but they taste great even when brine-cured. They make a great dressing, and serve them with pasta or even with capers.

Picholine

This olive which is shaped like a Torpedo hails from France and has a bright green color. They are crisp and crunchy with a tart and nut-like taste. They enhance the taste of any dish so eat them as you like!

Gordal

Coming from Spain, they drive their name Gordal due to their size. In Spanish, Gordal is used to refer to fat. Gordal olives are big in size and rich in texture. These olives are grown in Andalucia in a dry climate.

Alfonso

This is a big-deep purple to black colored olive that undergoes brine cure. They have a sour bitterness. Alfonsos are juicy, have a fleshy texture, and make a great dressing. They belong to Chili.

Mission

The US-based mission is the one most used for making olive oil. However, once they are brine-cured or dry-cured, they get a bright, mild, and grassy flavor making them suitable for use in dressing and food.

Manzanilla

Another type of olive hailing from Spain is Manzanilla. They have a bright green color and taste similar to smoked almonds. With the crispy texture they attain after being brine-cured, they are stuffed with pimientos. You can also serve it with crusty bread!

Beldi

Even though Morocco is known to produce several varieties of olive, only a few are exported and thus we get to taste a few only. Yet, if you can, grab your hands on Beldi. They have an intense flavor and are thus used in salads, tagines, and used in dishes to give them a great taste.

Amfissa

This Greece-origin black and green colored Amfissa’s a perfect treat for the taste buds. They are handpicked once they are ripe. Then they are brine-cured and ready to eat. They are best used in soups and stews, meats, and cheese!

After the death of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, the Muslim community got divided into two major sects Sunni and Shia. The Sunni sect is further divided into 4 schools of thought in Islam namely Hanafi, Malki, Shafi, and Hanbali.

It shall be made very clear that all Islamic schools make use of Quran and Hadith to provide a ruling on an issue. However, there are some issues that have not been clearly defined in the Quran and hadith and it is where these schools differ.

Unlike Sunni and Shia sects which treat each other wrong, All 4 Sunni schools of Islamic Fiqh consider each other correct. You can follow any of these 4 Sunni schools of Islamic Fiqh, and nobody is going to raise a question.

Hanafi

Hanafi school of Islamic Fiqh was founded by 
Imam Abu Hanifa
 an-Numan. He was a Merchant and use to spread Islamic knowledge in the city of Kufa, Iraq.

His major contribution to Islam is still alive and is known as Al Fiqh Al Akbar. 
The Hanafi School is the most famous and widely practiced one. It is followed in countries like Afghanistan, Turkey, Pakistan, Syria, Jordan, Lebanon, Iran, and Malaysia.

The Hanafi teachings and applications are the most flexible ones. It has kept things moderate and liberal upon issues that were not found in Quran and Hadith explicitly.

Maliki

The Maliki school of thought is the second most followed school by Muslims. About 25% of Muslims around the world follow it. It is mostly practiced in countries like North and West Africa, Sudan, Kuwait, Chad, Bahrain, UAE, and northern parts of Saudi Arabia.

The school was founded by 
Imam Malik Ibn Anas
 who belonged to the blessed city of Madinah. The 8
th
-century scholar, Imam Malik, used a different approach from the rest of the schools. 

According to him, the primary source of Islamic teachings is the Quran. Then we are to rely on the Sunnah of the Prophet PBUH. This sunnah is well visible from the practices of the people of Madinah as that was the place where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ resided and preached Islam.

Shafi

The Shafii school of thought has been developed and founded by 
Imam Shafi
 (767-820). He was a student of Imam Malik ibn Anas, yet he developed his own school of Fiqh later.

He wrote many books but the most notable are the ar-Risalah (‘the message’) and al-Umm (‘the mother’).

Countries like Kurdistan, Egypt, Yemen, Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, Palestine, Syria, Brunei, and Malaysia tend to implement and follow Shafi School of Fiqh.

The school differs from others as it relies less on Qiyas (collective consensus).

Hanbali

The Hanbali School was founded by an Iraqi scholar named 
Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
. Hanbal was a discipline of Shafii and used the Quran and Hadith to give out rulings. 

Today is the least practiced school as it is considered the most conservative. It is followed today in Saudi Arabia and Qatar. 
The school, however, is liberal in commercial matters.

Quranic regarding beating wives

Many people have misinterpreted the meaning of the following verse to claim that Islam allows husbands to beat their wives. Let me reproduce the verse; 

If you sense ill-conduct from your women, advise them ˹first˺, ˹if they persist,˺ do not share their beds, ˹but if they still persist,˺ then [as the last resort] 
beat
 them. – 
An-Nisa 4:34

Interpretation of the verse

1-
 Islam describes three levels of dealing with wives. 
If one’s wife is persistently misconducting with the husband, then he should 
advise her
 and make sure that matters get settled. 

2-
 However, if she does not agree then he can separate his bed and 
not sleep
 with her. 

3-
 However, if none of these make her realize her mistake, only then he can be a little harsher towards her. 
Disciplining one’s wife gently
 is the final resort. 

The earliest commentators understood that the beating was to be light enough not to leave a mark, should be done with nothing bigger than a tooth stick, and should not be on the face.

his wives

Aisha رضي الله عنها said: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ never beat anyone with his hand, neither a woman nor a servant. –

In a nutshell, Islam allows beating your wife gently but that too in extreme circumstances when you have exploited all other means to discipline her as explained in verse (4:34) of the Holy Quran.

People who come to Saudi Arabia on a family visit visa buy health insurance from their home country while stamping the visa on their passports. This is how a user claimed hospital expenses paid for the treatment of his father who came on a family visit visa to Saudi Arabia.

Conditions to claim Insurance

In order to claim medical insurance on a family visit visa, take care of the following 4 things;

Make sure that the 
visit visa insurance is valid
. 

It was an emergency case e.g. heart attack. 

The claim is submitted within 24 hours of admission.

The patient tried to approach a government hospital before heading to a private hospital.

Government v/s Private Hospital

As soon as you face a medical emergency, take your patient to the nearest government hospital for treatment. The government hospitals take emergency cases in a far better way 
without asking
 for the upfront payment and they are better trained to claim the bills from the insurance company. 

However, if the government hospital is not approachable, you can visit a private hospital and they would treat your patient.

Upfront Payment

The process to claim insurance on a family visit visa is 
not known
 to many private hospitals due to which they refuse to accept patients. 

Therefore, you would be required to pay an upfront deposit to cover medical expenses in case the insurance rejects the claim. 

In my case, I paid SR 20,000 deposit as my father required emergency heart surgery.

Contact the Insurance company

As soon as your family member is admitted to the hospital, push the hospital management to contact the insurance company and file a claim there. You can check the name of the insurance company through 
this link
. 

You are required to submit your first claim within 
24 hours
 of the patient being admitted to the hospital. 

Complaint to CHI

In case you feel that the insurance company is not cooperating or hesitating to approve the insurance claim, immediately
 file a complaint
 
to the Council of Health Insurance. 

If you know how things work in Saudi Arabia, I would suggest you file a complaint with CHI to be on the safer side. You can complain to CHI for a family visit visa holder through 
this link
.

Claim the Bills 

Keep a close follow-up with your hospital so that they keep on billing the insurance company for all the expenses. 

Otherwise, they might ask you to 
deposit another amount
 before the discharge or at least refuse to refund your initial deposit.

Keep in mind that whatever expenses are required for the treatment of a patient are approved by the insurance company. If the insurance company is not approving something, it means

Open an HDFC Bank NRI Account
Minimum balance Requirement

Opening an NRI bank account can be a grueling task only if you are not aware of the online banking options by HDFC. Online HDFC is a platform that you can access from anywhere even when you are in Saudi Arabia. 

The NRI (Non-Resident Indian) HDFC bank account can be opened and operated online only by following a simple guide and being equipped with all the necessary information.

Types of NRIs account by HDFC Bank

There are a number of NRI (Non-Resident Indian) accounts being offered by HDFC Bank.

NRE (Non-Resident External) Accounts

NRO (Non-Resident Ordinary) Accounts

FCNR (Foreign Currency Non-Resident) Accounts.

Difference in NRI accounts

Of course, these different accounts serve differently. NRE Accounts are best suited for those who want to have savings in their national currency i.e. Indian Rupee. On the other hand, the NRO Accounts are earning in the Indian rupee and wish to keep their savings in the Indian rupee. Lastly, the FCNR Accounts are ideal for those who wish to have saving in foreign currencies.

Thus, make up your mind before opening an NRI account and know the features of the above-mentioned one to avoid any complexities.

Required Documents

In order to open an NRE Savings Account with HDFC Bank from Saudi Arabia, here is the checklist of the documents required:

A readable photocopy of passport pages. All details such as personal information and passport details shall be readable. that display the applicant’s passport details and personal information

Copy of Permanent Account Number (PAN). In case PAN is not available, get a copy of Form 60.

Passport-sized photographs

Iqama or residence permit (photocopied)

Documents that verify that the oversea or the Indian address (address shall match the address on the application form)

Either an initial payment check or the draft from the applicant’s account. DD slip is mandatory if the draft is being used.

Open an HDFC Bank NRI Account

Now you can open an HDFC Bank NRE Account from Saudi Arabia through an online platform. For that, you need to fill out the 
online form
 available for the NRE/NRO account. Once the form is submitted, a representative from the HDFC bank will contact you and guide you through the process. If you are already a customer of HDFC bank, then you will have to attest the KYC documents yourself, otherwise, for new customers, KYC documents shall be attested by a designated authority.

Minimum balance Requirement

A minimum balance requirement has been set by HDFC Bank for the NRE (Non-Resident External) and NRO (Non-Resident Ordinary) accounts. Also, this minimum balance amount differs from location to location and branch to branch. As per the regulations, the Average Minimum Balance (AMB) For metro and urban branches is set at Rs.10,000, or a fixed deposit of Rs 1 Lakh for a minimum 1 year and 1 day period. AMB for semi-urban branches, set at Rs.5,000, or a fixed deposit of Rs 50,000 for a minimum 1 year and 1 day period. However, the Average Quarterly Balance (AQB) for rural branches is Rs.2,500, or a fixed deposit of Rs. 25,000 for a minimum 1 year and 1 day period.

Minimum balance requirements are subject to change and thus it is advised to stay updated. Also, you may be charged with fines and penalties in case you are not able to meet the AMB in your account!

Who was Anas Ibn Malik?
Anas Ibn Malik’s participations in wars
What makes Anas ibn Malik important?
Death of Prophet Muhammad
Death of Anas Ibn Malik

There are many Sahaba who had the privilege to serve Prophet Muhammad ﷺ but Anas ibn Malik رضي الله عنه is known as Khadim-e-Rasool.

Who was Anas Ibn Malik?

Anas ibn Malik ibn Nadar al-Khazraji Al-Ansari رضي الله عنه belongs to the Najjar clan of Khazraj. His father, Malik Ibn Nadr died as a non-Muslim. After that his mother, Umm Sulaim رضي الله عنها remarried Abu Talha ibn Thabit رضي الله عنه. 

Anas Ibn Malik رضي الله عنه was only 10 years old when Prophet Muhammad ﷺ migrated to Madinah in 622 AD. Anas ibn Malik was presented as a servant to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ by his mother and that’s why he is known as Khadim-e-Rasool Sahabi.

Anas Ibn Malik رضي الله عنه thus was raised by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and spent his early years with him. 

Anas Ibn Malik’s participations in wars

Anas Ibn Malik رضي الله عنه had participated in the 
Battle of Badr
 with Prophet Muhammad ﷺ at the age of only 12 years. 

In invasions like the 
Battle of Hunayn
, the 
Battle of Khyber
, and the conquest of Makkah, Anas played a significant role. He also participated in the battle of Qadisiyah.

What makes Anas ibn Malik important?

Anas Ibn Malik رضي الله عنه was only 10 years old when he was given to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. At that time, the ability to write was scarce. 

Yet Anas, at such a tender age, was able to write. Being close to the Holy Prophet PBUH, 2286 ahadith have been narrated by Anas Ibn Malik. He is known as a man of knowledge, patience, and honesty.

Death of Prophet Muhammad

 Prophet Muhammad ﷺ died in 632 AD so you must be wondering what happened to the Sahabi known as Khadim-e-Rasool? 

Anas Ibn Malik رضي الله عنه remained one of the most dutiful and prominent companions of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ even after his death. He was one of the greatest archers and made sure to uphold the mission of Islam.

He continued participating in the wars of conquest. He also played a part in conquering Iraq and Persia.

He was sent to Bahrain by the Caliph Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه for the collection of Zakat payment. On his return, the caliph passed away.

Anas Ibn Malik رضي الله عنه was blessed 
with 2 daughters and 8 sons.

Death of Anas Ibn Malik

Anas Ibn Malik رضي الله عنه died at the age of 103 years (lunar calendar) in Basra. His shrine has been simple and has been damaged over the years. It is visited by Muslims and is an important landmark in Islamic history. He was the 
last Sahabi to die
.

Police Inquiry

A Belgian was surprised at the check-in counter to know that they have not booked their infant’s ticket. 
Instead of buying a ticket, they decided to leave their ticket-less infant at the airport and get onboard for their Ryanair flight!

Not willing to buy the ticket

The police officer reported that the couple had left their son at the Ben-Gurion airport in Tel Aviv, Israel. The couple was equipped with their own tickets but neither had a ticket for their infant nor were willing to buy one!

Quoting the incident, the police officer said the couple refused to pay for their child’s ticket. They left the stroller, nested by their child, at the check-in desk and went to the passport control office.

Viral Video

A video also shows the shocking scene where the little boy is being left by his parents in the stroller at the check-in desk. Ryanair desk’s manager said that it was a surreal scene, he had never witnessed such before. He and his staff could not believe what they were seeing.

Thus, they contacted the police. The police found the parents, the abandoned child, and held an inquiry!

Police Inquiry

In the statement recorded by the police of the airport staff, the couple had arrived late for their flight. They did not have a ticket for the child and left him at the check-in desk.

The incident was reported on Tuesday, 31
st
 of January at the Ben Gurion International Airport. The couple was checking in for a Ryanair flight from Ben Gurion International Airport to Brussels, Belgium!

The couple could have booked an online ticket for their infant. As per Ryanair’s website, infants can get a reservation through online booking. An infant, who does not require a special seat, is charged €25 ($27).

The Israeli Airport Authority has confirmed the incident to CNN as well!

In the video, a man stands in a Saudi desert holding a alive catfish. 
The fish seems to hibernate in the desert in the summer season.

Catfish or Silver Fish

Dr. Ali Al-Sheikhi, the current CEO of Fisheries Sector Development, said it is a ‘catfish.’ Such a fish is known as a ‘silver fish’ or ‘qarmut fish’. It has 4 joints, its front head has an antenna-like structure, and a face similar to a cat’s.

It has false lungs

The main feature of the catfish is that they have false lungs, which enables them to live without water and on dry surfaces for about 8 hours. They are found in the lakes that are north of the equator.

Can live without water for 8 months

However, they are vulnerable in the summer and dry seasons. They can absorb moisture and lock it up in their silver shells. Thus enabling them to live without water for about 8 months. 

Thus, they are Fish, yet their bodies function like reptiles that can live in both water and on land. Their hibernation period is the time they seek shelter in water.

Dr. Ali Al-Sheikhi also briefed that the fish come to the land for food once the rain is over. It uses its tentacles to do so. This is why such fish is found in the deserts of Wadi al-Ramah.

Dr. Ibrahim Al-Harithi, a National Center for Wildlife Development marine ecologist, claims such a fish is a common sight in Asia, Europe, and South America. However, it has only been witnessed in Saudi Arabia at Wadi Hanifa and Wadi Al-Ramma.

He also said that fish has been introduced in Saudi Arabia for Fish farming. Many years from now, these fish were also introduced in the Wadi al-Rama. You can see them at the farms in the Qasim area. During floods, they move and get displaced.

Story of Prophet Dhul Kifl 

Prophet Al-Yasa عليه السلام
 (Elisha) wanted a successor for Bani Israel with a calm personality. Thus one day, Prophet Al-Yasa عليه السلام requested his companions to get assembled.

Prophet Dhul-Kifl عليه السلام tomb in Iraq

Prophet Al-Yasa 3 conditions

Prophet Al-Yasa عليه السلام then told that he was looking for a successor who would preach the message of Allah and fulfills the following 3 conditions;

He would fast in the daytime.

 Pass the night in prayers.

Not be angry with anyone.

Prophet Dhul Kifl acceptance

Upon hearing this, Prophet Dhul Kifl عليه السلام volunteered that he could be the next successor and would follow the conditions.

Prophet Al-Yasa عليه السلام asked thrice and repeated the condition of calmness and not getting angry. 

He
 accepted the conditions and thus after the death of Prophet Al-Yasa عليه السلام, he was appointed. 

He would preach the message of Allah to the people. He was a pious man who would fast in the daytime and pray at night. He was a very calm man who would not get angry.

This was something worrisome for the Devil. So, one day Iblis (the devil) asked his companions which one would go and make Ezekiel break his promise by making him angry. His companion named 
Abyaiz
 took the challenge of making Prophet Dhul-Kifl عليه السلام angry.

Abyaiz 1st visit

Abyaiz went to Prophet Dhul-Kifl عليه السلام during his nap time to make him angry. He knocked a the door disguised as an old man. He told that he was tortured and needed help. 

He welcomed him in and asked about his sufferings. Abyaiz stretched the story, on purpose so that his nap time would pass and he succeeded. 

Prophet Ezekiel عليه السلام patiently listened and asked him to visit him in the court in the evening so that justice can be done for him.

Sleepless Dhul Kifl waited for the old in the court in the evening, but he did not come.

Abyaiz 2nd visit

Abyaiz again came when Dhul Kifl was preparing to take a nap. Hazrat Dhul-Kifl عليه السلام allowed him to enter and inquired why he had not come to the court. He lied that he was forced not to go to court by torture. Abyaiz kept him busy until his sleep time was over.

He did not get a chance to sleep. He waited for Abyaiz in the court but he did not appear.

Iblis 3rd visit

Prophet Dhul-Kifl عليه السلام was very sleepy and thus asked that he should not be disturbed during his nap time. Abyaiz knocked on the door again and tried to disturb his sleep so he would not be able to fast, pray, and thought to make him angry.

When the family members did not let him enter, he appeared inside the house next to Dhul-Kifl’s room and started knocking at the door of his room.

Prophet Dhul-Kifl عليه السلام was able to realize that the man who entered the house without opening the door is actually Iblis. 

Iblis admitted that he was Iblis and said, “You have thwarted all my plans and frustrated all my efforts to entice you in my design. I intended to make you angry somehow so that one of your claims before Yasa could be proven false.”

Be thankful to Allah
Ask for forgiveness
Be Generous
Be conscious of Allah
Ask for Rizk from Allah

There is nothing wrong in generating wealth and we get 7 lessons from the life of Sahaba to increase wealth in an Islamic way.

No Interest

Interest tends to increase the wealth of the rich at the cost of decreasing that of the poor. Such an unjust business is unacceptable in Islam and thereby it forbids interest.

Allah destroys interest and enhances charity. Allah does not like sinning disbelievers. – 
Al-Baqarah 2:276

Dealing with interest is declaring war against Allah and Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. – 
Al-Ma’idah 5:33

Strengthen your family ties

Maintaining a stronger relationship with your family is a way to increase wealth as per Islam. 

How?
 
A person who is close to his family tends to be happier and makes better business decisions.

Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: Anyone who wants to have his provision expanded and his term of life prolonged should maintain ties of kinship. – 
Al-Adab Al-Mufrad 56

Be thankful to Allah

Being thankful to Allah is a sure way to increase your wealth as per Islam. 

How? 
When you are thankful for something, you are telling your mind that you are getting more than what you deserve. It gives your mind positive energy to make better decisions. 

If you are grateful, I will certainly give you more. – 
Ibrahim 14:7

Ask for forgiveness

Prophet Noah عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَامُ is reported to have said that those who seek forgiveness from Allah Almighty shall be blessed with rain from the skies and Allah shall increase them in wealth and bless them with children.

How? 
Seeking forgiveness indicates a humble attitude and it tells you that you are nothing. It helps you develop a hardworking attitude towards every matter in life including business.

Be Generous

Paying generously to poor people is another way to increase your wealth as per Islam. 

How? 
When you help someone and feel that you have been able to resolve one of their problems, your mind release dopamine (a chemical). You tend to be more satisfied in your life which leads to better decision-making.

Those who spend their wealth in the cause of Allah are that of a grain that sprouts into seven ears, each bearing one hundred grains. – 
Al-Baqarah 2:261

If you don’t have money, the food is free.

Be conscious of Allah

Being aware that Allah is watching you all the time is another way to increase your wealth as per Islam. 

How? 
Sometimes you tend to be lured by an opportunity that can make you quick money but could have a drastic impact later (if caught). You might think that you will not get caught in that wrongdoing and go for it. 
However, if you think that Allah is watching, you would not fall for that quick money and stay away from trouble in the long run.

Whoever is conscious of Allah, He will make a way out for them, and provide for them from sources they could never imagine. – 
At-Talaq 65:2-3

Ask for Rizk from Allah

Asking for your Rizq from Allah is a great way to increase your wealth as per Islam.

How? 
Seeking Allah’s help indicates a humble attitude and it tells you that you are nothing. It helps you develop a hardworking attitude towards every matter in life including business. 

Once the prayer is over, disperse throughout the land and seek the bounty of Allah. – 
Al-Jumu’ah 62:10
